description: Use for one product's current listing. Not for several ASINs (product_details_batch), seller offers or stock (offers_stock), or review text (product_reviews). Fetches the complete product record for one ASIN on one marketplace: title, price, star rating, rating count, images, description, feature bullets, variations and category. Price: $0.003 per call. 404 means the ASIN is absent from that marketplace and IS billed. 503 is a temporary failure on our side and is NOT billed - retry. Bullet points and specs are what Amazon shows for the listing; on multi-variant listings they can describe the product family rather than the exact variant. A null field means Amazon did not show it. Beside the price the record carries what the page shows there: `discount_percentage` (the saving against `product_original_price`, an integer), `product_price_per_unit` ("$0.59/fluid ounce"), `deal_badge` ("Limited time deal"), `coupon` and `promotion` in the page's own words, and `subscribe_and_save` -- `{price, price_per_unit, max_savings_price, max_savings_percentage}`, null when the listing has no such option. `return_policy` is the buy box's Returns line ("FREE refund/replacement until Jan 31, 2027"), and `buybox_winner.seller_url` is the seller's page. Three things a listing states are named at the top level: `whats_in_the_box` (the page's "What's in the box" list, an array of strings), `warranty` ("1 year manufacturer") and `ingredients` (the ingredient list as the page prints it); each is null when the listing states none. `product_information` still holds the same rows under the page's own labels. `product_photos` is this listing's whole gallery at full size, in the page's order (it used to hold one image, or thumbnails); other variants' images stay under `variation`. A page that comes back with no product on it is fetched again and, failing that, answered as the unbilled 503 -- never as an empty record. Keys of `product_information`, `tech_specs` and the other specification tables are trimmed: Amazon prints some rows twice, once with a trailing space ("Package Dimensions "), and the copies are merged under the clean name; when they differ the listing's own value wins (the second copy of "ASIN" on a variant often names the parent). `currency` is the symbol Amazon prints on the page ($, €, £, R$, AED); the ISO code is `price_snapshot.currency`. `is_best_seller` and `badges.best_seller` are true only for the listing's own "#1 Best Seller" badge. `ranks` and `category_path` are empty when Amazon's page for the listing shows no Best Sellers Rank rows or breadcrumb; a listing with the badge then gets one `ranks` entry read from the badge (rank 1 in the category the badge names), marked `source: best_seller_badge`.

asin.description: Single Amazon ASIN, 10 uppercase alphanumeric characters. Exactly one - comma-separated lists are rejected; use product_details_batch for many. An Amazon product URL (…/dp/ASIN) works too, in place of an ASIN; lower case is fine. A URL's domain sets the marketplace unless geo says otherwise.
asin.title: Asin

compact.description: Return the compact record (about 4 KB: identity, price with its discount, unit price, deal, coupon and Subscribe & Save, rating, availability, return policy, box contents, warranty, ingredients, bullets, category, offer, buy box). false returns the full record (about 75 KB, includes from_manufacturer, tech_specs, product_information, product_reviews).
compact.title: Compact

fields.description: Comma-separated top-level fields to return instead of the compact set, e.g. "tech_specs,product_information". Any response lists what it left out under _omitted_fields.
fields.title: Fields
